# Monsters

Monsters come in crowds just off-screen around every player, more as the player's level rises (planning/modules/match.md), and drop a gem worth their `xp` when they die. Each is one file in src/content/monsters/: data plus an optional behavior.
- **Behavior:** without one, a monster heads for the nearest player, fanned out a little so a crowd doesn't stack (Dot, the only monster so far). A monster with its own way to move or attack has a `think`, run on the server every tick, and an optional `onDeath`; its `description` says what it does (under "What exists now", `think: (code)` marks a monster with a behavior of its own). A new way to move or attack is a new behavior.
- **What a behavior can use:** its own movement, projectiles and fields of its own aimed at players, statuses on players, spawning other monsters, dropping pickups, effects. Its private state goes in its `mem`; what players must see (it is winding up, it is shielded) goes in its 4 synced `slots`, and its look reads them.
- **Numbers:** `hp` (grows with the level of the player it spawned around), `speed` (units per second; players move at 210), `radius`, `damage` (per second while touching a player), `xp`, `weight` (how often it spawns compared with the others; 0: only when another monster or an event spawns it), `fromLevel` (the first player level it spawns around).
- **Look:** a critter: a shape, a warm color (red, orange, purple, pink) and a face: `mood` (angry, happy, calm or scared), 1 to 3 `eyes`, a `mouth` (none, o, smile, frown or teeth). Monsters are angry unless their face says otherwise.

## The bar for a new monster
- **A behavior no existing monster has:** a new way to move, attack, survive, or deal with players or other monsters. New hp, speed, size, shape or color on an existing behavior is not a new monster. Use the descriptions under "What exists now".
- **It makes you move differently.** A player in its crowd dodges, chases, keeps away or holds still where Dot's crowd wouldn't make them.
- **It reads at a glance:** its shape and face tell it apart in a crowd of others, and its look warns before it acts (its face or a mark changes first), so a player can answer by moving.
- **It counts what it adds.** Monsters it spawns and shots it fires add to a crowd of up to 60 around each player: say how many at most. Shots fired in numbers move by a path (planning/modules/upgrades.md).
- **At most 10 monster types** (ones with `weight` 0 don't count). Past that, the same task (or one before it) removes or merges one and says which.

## A task that adds or changes a monster
Next to the usual sections, it has:
- Its exact numbers (hp, speed, radius, damage, xp, weight, fromLevel) and its look: shape, color, face, and how the look changes before it acts.
- What counters it, and what it punishes (a build, a habit).
- **## Compared with what exists:** a table with one row for every monster with a similar behavior, and every monster it names as similar:

| Existing | What it shares | What the new one does that it can't (not numbers) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dot | heads straight for the nearest player | ... |

A missing row, or a row whose difference is only numbers, gets the task rejected by the architect.
